mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing consumer and business spending. This should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which can lead to economic downturns and negative equity returns. This should result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days when the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.2 percentage points.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following a rising UNRATE signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a rising HOUST signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production indicates strong economic activity, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days when INDPRO is above 100.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a high INDPRO signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a strong labor market signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High real consumer spending indicates strong demand, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 5-day windows following a high RSAFS signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index in a late-cycle expansion indicates inflationary pressures, which could lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a rising CPIAUCSL signal in a late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate and low unemployment indicates a tightening monetary policy, which should lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a tightening monetary policy signal, the hypothesis is rejected.
